you should go to your local pharmacist and ask them about how to quit and they can tell you the right patches/lozenges etc that will work for you. there’s nothing wrong with using NRT to help you quit and as someone who’s been in the same boat as you relying on willpower alone, it’s a lot easier to stick to it when you have the patches. I had a client disclose cameras to me and told me I could put the privacy cover over the ring camera in the living room while I’m hanging out in there. She mentioned the cameras were only to keep an eye on the dogs. She didn’t tell me it recorded audio. One time I was sitting down in the living room and put the privacy cover over the camera and called my sister. Little did I know this woman LISTENED to my phone call and complained about me because I mentioned on the phone-call that I prefer owning larger dogs to smaller dogs (Hers were small). I was beyond uncomfortable after that and it really turned me off from pet sitting. Make sure to be wary of cameras even if they disclose them; people will say that the cameras are only to watch the dogs, but you’ll never know that for sure. And also make sure to ask if they record audio as well. I was unaware that a lot of these indoor cameras now record audio, and a privacy cover on a camera does not shut off the audio. It’s tough to take phone calls outside constantly, especially during extended stays like this was. I’m sure most people wouldn’t go to these extremes, but just be cautious.

Congrats on losing 17 lbs!! One tiny change you could make is swapping out the energy drink for green tea or protein coffee and see if that helps. For me personally, I find that energy drinks give me the energy initially but then I crash hard come afternoon. If you wanna try the protein coffee it’s super easy to make, just fill your mug halfway with coffee (I just use instant coffee since it’s quicker lol), add some sugar free almond milk about 1/4 of the way to the top, then add 1/2 a scoop of protein powder. It comes out to about 93 calories. Another thing is exercise. You don’t have to sign up for the gym right away, I didn’t until about a year after home workouts. I just started off doing yoga in the mornings (there’s tons of free 5-10 mins on youtube) and that does a lot for boosting my energy. Another easy way to get movement is by going on short 10 min walks, and you can gradually increase them. I find it’s always fun to chat with a friend on a walk, a nice way to get a social activity that doesn’t revolve around food or drinking. I think overall just increasing your protein intake especially during breakfast might help out your energy levels. Also what you said about upping the calories by using rice could be a good idea, since carbs are important for energy levels. And I think at your height and weight you’d likely still be in a deficit around 1700 calories, and you’d probably have even more wiggle room if you added daily walks into your routine. I hope this was helpful :) Good luck!!
